item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q006_ubiquitin_like_function_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, ubiquitin-related proteins, UBX domains, and Ras-binding domains are three separate families under the same homologous superfamily: family d.15.1.1 “Ubiquitin-related” (SUNID 54237), family d.15.1.2 “UBX domain” (SUNID 54250), and family d.15.1.5 “Ras-binding domain, RBD” (SUNID 54263) are all children of the d.15.1 “Ubiquitin-like” superfamily (SUNID 54236). That superfamily sits in the d.15 “beta-Grasp (ubiquitin-like)” fold inside class d, alpha and beta proteins (a+b). SCOPe’s homology scope treats the d.15.1 superfamily, but not the broader d.15 fold, as implying homology. The useful inference is therefore remote common ancestry and a shared beta-grasp/ubiquitin-like structural core between ubiquitin-related, UBX, and RBD domains; they can be related templates for that core. The unsafe transfer is the specific family-level biochemical annotation: an RBD hit should not by itself annotate ubiquitin conjugation or UBX/p97-adaptor function, and a UBX or ubiquitin-like hit should not by itself imply Ras binding. Loops, binding surfaces, and terminal conjugation motifs must be established with family-level or direct evidence rather than copied merely because all three are in d.15.1.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ubiquitin&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=UBX&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Ras-binding&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236/children?limit=50","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54235/homology"]}]}
